source_excerpts.text:
I constructed a path-ensemble representation that supplies an exact cooperative source–sink law and a computable energy bound without enumerating the module’s configuration graph. It works for the original hard two-dimensional Kob–Andersen model at \(p=0.80\).
The quantitative result is nevertheless too weak:
\[ \boxed{10^{-11593}\le D(0.80)\le 0.238144.} \]
This is not an informative prediction. Positivity at high density was already established, and existing specialised results have much stronger asymptotic scope. The advance here is in constructing and accounting for the module, not in resolving dense cooperative transport. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/html/2003.08495v2)
The strongest preserved operation replaces a list of microscopic histories with exact laws for the probability transported by those histories. Those laws compose through the construction and control congestion. A separate calculation identifies why the resulting full-frame representation remains quantitatively unsuitable.
cray_compressed_transport_bundle.zip  
A compact path description does not, by itself, give a compact transport certificate.
A legal route can be short while an enormous number of initial configurations funnel through the same intermediate transition. That multiplicity determines the current’s energy. Storing the route as a loop or recursive program does not remove it.
I examined three alternatives. Deterministic path compression retained a factorial history penalty. Quotienting configurations by vacancy count discarded information needed to establish legality. Randomising paths helped only after choosing the randomisation so that its entire transported probability law could be calculated.
The resulting representation attaches three objects to a path-generating operation:
\[ \text{exact source and endpoint law}, \qquad \text{legal microscopic implementation}, \qquad \text{second-moment bound}. \]
The second moment measures concentration relative to equilibrium. It replaces a worst-case count of inverse histories.
This does not invent cooperative paths, frameability or information-loss analysis. Those are established ingredients in specialised KA methods. The contribution candidate is the explicit density calculation and its composition into a finite certificate. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/html/2003.08495v2)

The report derives a closed sectorwise energy formula with \(O(m)\) summands. The direct implementation gives:
These are measured calculations in this container, not general performance guarantees. The length-256 calculation does not enumerate its \(2^{512}\) binary configurations.
The underlying empty-column manoeuvre is established geometry. The compressed current formula, its conserved normalisation and its exact energy contraction are the objects developed here. They provide an additional primitive for future compositions rather than a dense diffusion result by themselves. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2003.02531?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
The previous module’s gate became too rare because it required favourable arrangements in a fixed \(3\times3\) block. The new gate is recursive and remains independent of its port occupation.
For gate evaluation, replace the designated port by an occupied site. Every vacancy test then depends only on the reservoir.
A square has a frame when its left column and bottom row are empty. A \(2\times2\) seed is good when it contains at least three vacancies. With at most one forced occupied site,
\[ f_2=q^3 \]
is a valid probability lower bound.
For a square of side \(2n\), split it into four \(n\)-square children. A child is successful when it is good and can expand to the parent by alternating horizontal and vertical additions. Every newly annexed strip must contain a vacancy. The parent gate is the union of the four successful-child events.
For a right or upward addition, move the old empty frame line beside the fresh strip, perform the balanced rotation, then undo the temporary frame movement.
For a left or downward addition, rotate the fresh strip beside the existing empty frame line and exchange the two occupation lines.
The enlarged rectangle has the required frame. All supporting vacancies lie inside the module. An occupied exterior is allowed.
The old empty-column operations make this geometry possible; the new probability calculation does not treat them as new inventions. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.02531)
The newly annexed strip lengths are \(k\) and \(k+1\), for \(k=n,\ldots,2n-1\). A conservative extension probability is
\[ r_n= \frac{1-p^{n-1}}{1-p^n} \prod_{k=n}^{2n-1}(1-p^k)(1-p^{k+1}). \tag{4} \]
The prefactor accounts for the protected occupied port when it lies outside the selected child.

source.range_scope: Full density/energy costs, p=.8 weak bound and practical limits.

source_excerpts.text:
The remaining question is whether the implicit current’s energy can also be bounded without expanding its histories.
Let \(\rho_t\) be the density, relative to equilibrium, of the unnormalised positive-source measure at microscopic clock \(t\). A direct antisymmetrisation and Cauchy–Schwarz argument gives
\[ \boxed{ \mathbb E\sum_b w_bH_b^2 \le16T^2\sup_t\mathbb E\rho_t^2, } \tag{7} \]
where \(T\) bounds the path length and \(w_b\le4\) accounts for overlapping modules.
The task is therefore to derive the density bound, not supply it as an assumption.
For one framed block, define
\[ R_L(p)= 16\prod_{k=2}^{L-1} \max\{1,V_k(p)\}\max\{1,V_{k+1}(p)\}. \tag{8} \]
The factor 16 bounds the seed preparation. The remaining factors come from the exact strip moments. During a strip rotation, the additional factor is at most \(L^2\).
The proof also pays for information that could otherwise be hidden:
Seed selection. There are at most
\[ S=L^4/16 \]
pairs of seed locations. Their contributions are bounded without enumerating pivot histories.
Prepared port positions. There are at most \(N^2\) position pairs, where
\[ N=2L^2. \]
Conditioning on these positions makes each middle transposition word a fixed permutation.
The simulated occupied port. One simulated occupied token represents an actual vacancy. Forgetting its location costs an explicit factor \(N^2q/p\) in squared density. It is not treated as a free label.
Inverse preparation. The full port-transposition word is palindromic. Its reversal has the same history probability when started from the opposite port assignment. This controls the return phase without pretending that the program’s random history disappears for free.
These estimates give
\[ \sup_t\mathbb E\rho_t^2 \le S^2N^6L^2\frac qp\,R_L(p)^2. \tag{9} \]
A uniform microscopic length bound is
\[ T=256L^3. \]
Writing \(\gamma=\mathbb Eg\), the resulting module cost satisfies
\[ \boxed{ C_L(p)\le \frac{8T^2S^2N^6L^2R_L(p)^2}{p^2\gamma^2}. } \tag{10} \]
The earlier nonlocal completion supplies its explicit coarse energy factor \(\mathcal K(b)\), with \(b=1-\gamma\). Substituting a certified gate lower bound \(f\le\gamma\) gives
\[ \boxed{ D(p)\ge \frac{p^2f^2} {8T^2S^2N^6L^2R_L(p)^2\mathcal K(1-f)}. } \tag{11} \]
Every term is obtained from finite scalar calculations. No unknown spectral gap, supplied completion-error bound, global corrector or affordable invers
